messages:
erin: Quick question — we need a short, actionable playbook for low-precision benchmark runs (FP8/INT8/4-bit). Specifically: kernel selection, batching heuristics, KV‑cache priming/warmup, calibration effects on perf vs quality, tokenization parity, and powercap handling. What edge cases tripped us before?

sam: +1. Main surprises were: runtime picking a slower INT8 kernel for short sequences, and KV cache cold-start costs on chat workloads. Also tokenization differences across tokenizers caused small but measurable token-count deltas. :thinking:

joseph: Agreed. For kernel selection we should force a deterministic mapping in the benchmark harness: prefer kernel X for transposed matmuls on >=512 seq, fallback to kernel Y for <512. Otherwise noise from auto selection makes comparisons unfair.

maya: Adding my notes from last run: warmup needs to be measured in both tokens and wall time. Example command I used:

```
./bench/run_single.sh \
  --model redwood-7b \
  --quant-mode int8 \
  --kernel-policy "prefer_fast_for_long_seq" \
  --batching dynamic \
  --warmup-tokens 5000 \
  --inference-tokens 20000 \
  --powercap 250
```

Results (local A100 80GB):
```
warmup: 5000 tokens (primed kv cache)
steady: tokens/s 720
latency mean 52ms p95 140ms
compared to fp16: throughput 0.88x, latency 0.95x
```

maya: Note: if you only do warmup by time (e.g., 30s) we saw different effective token counts depending on batching. Always specify warmup-tokens.

priya: Calibration caveat: per-channel min/max calibration for INT8 that uses a small calibration set can slightly change generation distribution. For quality-sensitive evals, keep the same seed/inputs and measure delta on a fixed eval set (exact-match and rouge). For perf-only runs you can skip heavy calibration but document it.

sam: Batching heuristics: dynamic batching with a max-batch of 8 + latency SLO is usually fair. But for low-precision, larger batches can push a different kernel path (fused matmul) which is not available in FP16 run — that creates unfair wins. So benchmark config should either enable the same kernel family across precisions or report kernel family in metadata.

erin: Good point — include kernel_family and kernel_version fields in bench metadata (we'll add to harness). Also how do we handle tokenization parity?

joseph: Always run the same tokenizer binary/version and record tokenizer version/hash. Even different whitespace normalization changes token counts. If you must compare across tokenizers, normalize to codepoints and compare token counts in a separate column.

maya: Quick trick to measure KV-cache cold-start: run N short chats that each use fresh session ids, measure first-token latency vs subsequent ones. Example snippet:

```
for i in {1..20}; do 
  session=$(uuidgen)
  ./call_infer --session $session --prompt "Hello" --tokens 64
done
```

Collect first-token latency and median of subsequent tokens. Report cold-start ratio.

priya: Powercap: include both an uncapped run and a run with the operational power target (e.g., 200W). Sometimes quantized kernels are more memory-bandwidth bound and respond differently to power limiting. Always report GPU power and fan state.

sam: On profiling: capture kernel timeline + nvprof/perf + flamegraph of host threads. Small example of what to log in metadata: {model, quant_mode, kernel_policy, batching_mode, warmup_tokens, powercap_watts, tokenizer_hash, gpu_type, driver_version, cuda_version}.

benchmark-bot: scheduled bench 1798765400 for redwood-7b INT8 on a100-80gb (config id: bp-179876). Will post artifacts to gs://redwood-bench/bp-179876.

erin: Nice. Action items: Sam — write a benchmark harness patch that forces kernel_family and emits metadata. Joseph — add kv cold-start microbenchmark to bench suite. Priya — document calibration/quality checklist. Maya — add warmup-by-tokens option and a powercap test. I'll collate into a short playbook.

sam: I'll open a PR with the harness changes today, will include sample output format and an example artifact.

joseph: I'll add a small reproducible notebook that runs the cold-start loop and plots first-token vs steady token latency.

maya: One last thing: add an explicit note to not compare runs where batcher changed from "fixed" to "dynamic" unless you include both configs in table. We lost 12% once because the batcher auto-switched.

erin: Perfect. I'll draft the playbook and ping the group when it's ready. Thanks all :rocket:
